correctness.rationale: The complete-sweep matrix follows from three exact scalar coordinate equations. Its two-column Gram trace is rho^2 S(rho), determinant rho^4(1+2rho^2), and det(I-G)=(rho-1)(6rho^4+2rho^2-rho-1), all established by explicit polynomial multiplication and independently verified coefficient-by-coefficient in the embedded standard-library code. The strictly convex quartic has precisely two roots in the SPD range. On the central interval, determinant G<272/729<1 excludes both Gram eigenvalues exceeding one; outside it, det(I-G)<0 forces one above one. Equality and condition-number transforms are exact. The verifier replay reports 5520 checks. Infinite parameter assertions rely on the exact analytic polynomial argument, never on numerical sampling.

The assessed statement is the complete Euclidean singular-norm/nonexpansion classification on the entire SPD equicorrelation range, with two distinct sign-dependent sharp condition-number thresholds and a fixed-condition-number witness. value.rationale: This is a natural complete phase classification for the canonical dense three-coordinate equicorrelation SPD family, not a free parameter slice. It establishes two distinct, sharp condition-number frontiers for Euclidean error amplification despite the same SPD energy descent and the same spectral condition number. The exact rational condition-six sign reversal shows why conditioning alone is insufficient for choosing a transient-error guarantee. The nonlinear Gram determinant and two-root sign structure are structurally informative in the smallest dimension allowing the complex nonzero cyclic-sweep spectrum. The statement is self-contained and benchmarkable without claiming broader all-SPD minimax results.
